'''Walter Selke''' (11 May 1947 – 22 December 2023<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aachen-gedenkt.de/traueranzeige/walter-selke|title=Traueranzeigen von Walter Selke, Aachen gedenkt|language=de|access-date=2024-04-16|publisher=www.aachen-gedenkt.de}}</ref>) was a German  professor for [[Theoretical Physics]] at the [[RWTH Aachen]].

==Career==
After receiving his doctoral degree at the [[Leibniz University Hannover]], followed by postdoctoral positions at the [[Saarland University]], [[Cornell University]], and [[Boston University]], he became a permanent scientific staff member of [[Forschungszentrum Jülich]] in 1981. He held a similar position at the [[Rüschlikon|IBM Research Center (Zürich)]] in 1985–1986. In 1996 Selke became a university professor at the [[RWTH Aachen]], and from 2008 was engaged in the ''Jülich Aachen Research Alliance'' ([[RWTH Aachen|JARA]]). He retired from his teaching duties in 2012.

Selke's main field of expertise was [[statistical physics]], with applications especially, to [[magnetism]] and [[surface physics]]. 
He was best known for his work on
[[commensurability (mathematics)|commensurate]] and incommensurate [[ANNNI model|spatially modulated superstructures]] in [[solid-state physics|solids]], with realizations in [[magnet]]s, [[ferroelectric]]s, [[alloy]]s and [[adsorbate]] systems.

Selke published about 150 scientific papers in journals, conference proceedings, [[monograph]]s and books, including many [[review article]]s. Among his coauthors are [[Kurt Binder]], [[Michael E. Fisher]], and [[Valery Pokrovsky]]. He organized and co-organized several workshops and conferences, such as a series of meetings in the years 1988 to 1997 with physicists from the [[Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics]], which took place alternately in Germany and Russia.

From 1997 to 2000 he was member of the editorial board of the [[Journal of Statistical Physics]]. In the inaugural year 2008 he was named an 'Outstanding Referee' by the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.aps.org/OutstandingReferees|title=Physical Review Journals - Outstanding Referees|language=en|access-date=2024-04-16|publisher=journals.aps.org}}</ref> In 2009, he held a guest professorship at the [[University of New South Wales]].
